questions.solution_html:

questions.question: Write a short note on the importance of early intervention in depression.
questions.solution_html:
• Early intervention in depression is crucial to prevent the condition from worsening and leading to
  • severe outcomes such as suicidal thoughts or substance abuse ((2 marks))
  • Identifying symptoms like persistent sadness, fatigue, or loss of interest at an early stage allows
  • timely counseling and treatment. Support from family, teachers, and peers helps adolescents cope
  • better and recover faster ((2 marks))
  • ((2 Marks))
  • Causes : Major causes include lack of sex education, peer pressure, early sexual activity, poverty
  • and absence of parental guidance. In some cases, abuse or coercion also contributes ((3 Marks))
  • Consequences : The consequences are both physical and psychological — complications during
  • childbirth, higher maternal and infant mortality rates, school dropout, and social stigma. Teenage
  • mothers often face emotional stress, economic hardship, and limited job opportunities ((3 Marks))
  • Preventive strategies : include comprehensive sex education, promoting contraception awareness
  • and empowering adolescents to make informed reproductive choices ((2 Marks))
questions.final_answer: and empowering adolescents to make informed reproductive choices ()
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Discuss the importance of vocational counselling in career planning.
questions.solution_html:
• Vocational counselling assists adolescents in understanding their strengths, interests, and aptitudes
  • enabling them to make appropriate career choices. It guides them in exploring job opportunities
  • acquiring necessary skills, and setting realistic career goals ((2 marks))
  • Proper counselling reduces confusion, enhances motivation, and ensures better job satisfaction in
  • the long term ((2 marks))
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025

questions.question: Write short notes on the role of career talks in motivating adolescents.
questions.solution_html:
• Career talks expose adolescents to various career options, inspiring them through real-life success
  • stories and professional experiences. These talks enhance awareness about emerging fields
  • educational requirements, and skill development ((2 marks))
  • They motivate students to set goals, plan their future, and work with confidence and purpose (2
  • marks)

questions.question: Explain how emotional intelligence helps in building relationships.
questions.solution_html:
• Emotional intelligence (EI) involves recognizing, understanding, and managing one’s own emotions
  • and those of others ((2 marks))
  • High EI enables adolescents to communicate effectively, empathize, and manage conflicts
  • positively. It fosters trust, cooperation, and deeper emotional bonds, strengthening friendships and
  • family relationships ((2 marks))

questions.question: Describe four signs of media addiction in adolescents.
questions.solution_html:
• Four signs of media addiction include excessive time spent online, neglect of studies or social
  • interactions, irritability when disconnected from devices, and sleep disturbances ((2 marks))
  • Overuse of social media or gaming can lead to anxiety, reduced concentration, and social isolation

questions.question: Discuss the characteristics of adolescence in detail.
questions.solution_html:
• Adolescence : Adolescence is the transitional stage between childhood and adulthood, marked by
  • rapid physical, emotional, and cognitive changes ((2 Marks))
  • Physical and emotional changes : Physically, puberty brings hormonal changes, growth spurts, and
  • development of secondary sexual characteristics. Emotionally, adolescents experience mood
  • swings, identity exploration, and self-consciousness. Socially, peer relationships become highly
  • influential, and there is a desire for independence from parents ((4 marks))
  • Cognitively, abstract thinking and decision-making abilities develop, but emotional regulation may
  • still be immature. This stage is crucial for shaping personality, values, and mental well-being (4
  • marks)
